question: For the line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{-1}=\frac{z-3}{2}$ and the plane $2x+y-2z=-7$, determine the acute angle between the line and the plane and hence obtain the coordinates of their point of intersection.
explanation:
Angle Between the Line and the Plane
The direction ratios of the line are $2,-1,2$, so a direction vector is
$$\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$$
A normal vector to the plane is
$$\vec{n}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$$
If $\phi$ is the acute angle between the line and the plane, then
$$\sin\phi=\frac{|\vec{b}\cdot\vec{n}|}{|\vec{b}||\vec{n}|}$$
Now,
$$\vec{b}\cdot\vec{n}=2(2)+(-1)(1)+2(-2)=-1$$
Also,
$$|\vec{b}|=3,\quad |\vec{n}|=3$$
Therefore,
$$\sin\phi=\frac{1}{9}$$
Hence,
$$\phi=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)$$

Point of Intersection
Let the common ratio in the Cartesian equation of the line be $t$. Then
$$x=1+2t,\quad y=-2-t,\quad z=3+2t$$
Since the point of intersection lies on the plane,
$$2(1+2t)+(-2-t)-2(3+2t)=-7$$
Simplifying,
$$-6-t=-7$$
Hence, $t=1$. Therefore,
$$x=3,\quad y=-3,\quad z=5$$

Final Result
The acute angle between the line and the plane is $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)$, and their point of intersection is $(3,-3,5)$.
